open_points.subject: service_invoker.prepare_request pre-send validation
open_points.text: State 2 orders “the instance or its address is missing or not allowed, or a required header is repeated or invalid ... or its credential cannot be resolved ...; an input value cannot be placed”, while State 5 lists “a repeated required header, a plain `http` target not allowed, then the credential, then input placement” and omits `required_header_invalid`.
open_points.question: Does `prepare_request` check invalid required headers, and what exact order applies among `plain_http_not_allowed`, `required_header_repeated`, and `required_header_invalid`?
options: Check instance selection, address, repeated header, invalid header, plain HTTP, credential, then input placement
Check instance selection, address/plain-HTTP policy, repeated header, invalid header, credential, then input placement
Do not recheck invalid required headers at send time
open_points.default_guess: Check instance selection, address, repeated header, invalid header, plain HTTP, credential, then input placement.

open_points.subject: runs.capture_failed_execution
open_points.text: State 3 says “`runs` copies a spooled file ... only after every check of the capture has passed ... so a refused capture copies nothing”; State 5 instead makes an exception for “bytes a capture copied before `functions` refused the case” and says the operation copies inputs before calling `functions.add_captured_trial_case`.
open_points.question: May a refused capture leave unreferenced bytes in the content-addressed area, or must every possible `functions` refusal be checked before copying?
options: Precheck every capture and case condition before copying, so refusal leaves no bytes
Copy first and permit unreferenced bytes when `functions` later refuses
Make copying and case creation one atomic store change
open_points.default_guess: Precheck every condition before copying so a refused capture leaves no bytes.

open_points.subject: store.read_records and store.record_change
open_points.text: `store.read_records` says “records are never edited (A01 rule 6)”, while Named store changes says “a lifecycle change ... updates those fields of the entity's one record in place”.
open_points.question: Which records and fields may be updated in place, and what immutability guarantee must `store.read_records` and `record_change` enforce?
options: Only the listed lifecycle fields of entity records may change; all other facts and all immutable value/trace records cannot change
No record changes in place; every lifecycle transition creates a new record
Any entity field may change when its owning module requests it
open_points.default_guess: Permit in-place updates only to the explicitly listed lifecycle fields of entity records.

open_points.subject: store.page_records continuation tokens
open_points.text: The token is “the store position of the last item returned” and is refused when it “names no position of that list”, but filters include mutable lifecycle fields such as `status`, whose value may change between pages.
open_points.question: What happens when the record anchoring a continuation token no longer matches the token's status or other mutable-field filter when the next page is requested?
options: Accept the token as a global store-position anchor and continue below it under the current filter
Reject it because its anchor is no longer a member of the filtered list
Preserve a snapshot of filtered membership for the lifetime of the token
open_points.default_guess: Accept it as a global store-position anchor bound to the record type and filter, even if the anchor no longer matches.

open_points.subject: store.spool_file recovery after an unrecorded read output
open_points.text: `store.spool_file` makes a completed file visible and “a completed file is never overwritten”; the response file is spooled before `record_read_outcome`, while “changes the request made before [a failed store change] stay”. No rule says what happens to that unrecorded file when recovery retries the same `read` element with the same next attempt number.
open_points.question: If `record_read_outcome` fails after a read response file was spooled, how does recovery handle the existing file when the retried read returns the same or different bytes for the same SpooledFile identity?
options: Remove files not referenced by a concluded record before retrying the element
Reuse an existing file only when its digest matches and fail otherwise
Reserve or record the read attempt before spooling so a retry uses a new identity
open_points.default_guess: Remove unrecorded files for that element and attempt before retrying the read.

open_points.subject: effects.grant_standing_approval
open_points.text: Its Observable effect says “Later sends of that node in runs of that version need no approval”, but M25 and A10 say grants for `read` or `draft-write` are never used and every resend after `not_applied` requires a fresh approval even when a grant exists.
open_points.question: What exact promise should the grant operation make about later sends?
options: It bypasses approval only for eligible `state-transition` and `external-effect` sends, excluding every resend after `not_applied`
It bypasses approval for every non-destructive send, including resends after `not_applied`
Refuse grants for `read` and `draft-write` nodes because they have no effect
open_points.default_guess: Apply the established exceptions: only eligible state-transition and external-effect sends are covered, never a resend after `not_applied`.
